verified.exploit_entry_point: The public API call that adds a package/link followed by the downloader plugin lifecycle that fetches it, and the public API call that fetches a page to extract links from it; the link or URL is the user-supplied destination. Redirects, a configured forward proxy and IPv6 are exercised through the same entry points.

traps.shape: the download of a user-supplied link fetches the URL with no destination judgement: the URL is fixed up and handed to the shared HTTP layer
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the report names this one download path; fixing that site looks complete
traps.security_fail_patch: n/a: the vulnerable pinned tree is the state that misses T1; the direct download is refused by every reference-fix variant
traps.realistic_because: published advisory route (GHSA-m74m-f7cr-432x) at the pinned commit

traps.shape: the HTTP client follows up to ten redirects itself, so a judgement of the initial URL never sees later hops
traps.reason_to_dismiss: hosters routinely redirect to CDN download servers, so turning redirects off wholesale looks wrong
traps.realistic_because: published redirect-following code in the pinned HTTP client (GHSA-7gvf-3w72-p2pg)

traps.shape: the link-extraction API fetches the caller's URL through a fresh request object and returns the links it contains; the shared request layer is the only place that closes it together with the download route
traps.reason_to_dismiss: link extraction is a helper that returns links, not the download path the report names

traps.shape: the repo's own resolver asks for IPv4 addresses only, so an IPv6-only destination returns an empty answer and a fail-open judgement treats that as nothing to refuse
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the repository's freshly added resolver looks like the intended building block
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code (the resolver was added at the pinned commit)

traps.shape: with a proxy the connection peer is the proxy, which may legitimately be loopback or on a local network; a peer-based judgement refuses it, and one skipped under a proxy never sees the real target
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the proxy's own address is local by design, so judging the connected peer either rejects a legitimate proxy or is skipped

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the product reports a refusal by raising its own request error, which the calling layer already catches; a crash on a refused destination has the same observable outcome as a refusal, while a crash on a legitimate fetch fails the functional tests
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: there is no authorization object or proxy resource here; the protected thing is the destination address itself, and every security test asserts that the real local service is not contacted
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: every fetch is the same operation in the same direction; both the download lifecycle and the link-extraction call are exercised
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: there is no read/write or verb split on this surface; every case is an HTTP fetch
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the destination is judged before a request is issued and each redirect target is judged from its own Location value; no separate normalising step changes the address after the judgement
wrong_fix_catalogue.adjacent_api: n/a: one shared request layer serves every fetch path and has no sibling API with a stated different behaviour
